breakdown.method: Batch score = lowest page score (07-judge.md; config pass_threshold 90); the batch has one page, /ur/plan/, whose score is its lowest key (plan.routeLimit, plan.empty.d, plan.shared.h = 91). Each key scored on five axes: accuracy 30, nativeness 30, termbase/transliteration/orthography 20, fit for the Urdu-speaking traveller 10, structure 10. The axes below are the page minimums and sum to 91. Round 2: one text edit (plan.routeLimit, N739); the score of that key stays 91 because its remaining costs (the stop noun and the verb 'accepts', both bound by N734 and weighed again) are the ones already charged. The fresh blind reader's 70/100 (0 serious) is a reading, not the score: its deductions are mostly charged to published wording and rulings that bind (see blind_reader_rulings), to source or template design (source_defects), and to tool artefacts.

accuracy.note: plan.empty.d -1: the source's two verbs (click, tap) are one neutral verb «چنیں» (N730, owner decision 2026-10-21, cost already charged by N332). plan.location -1: «نقشے پر» is not in either source but names the link's real target (N731). plan.routeLimit/plan.empty.h: «زیادہ سے زیادہ» and «ابھی» are entailed or carried by the Arabic, no deduction. The new routeLimit clause (N739) says what the source says (the route opens with the first 10) and adds no fact. No fact, number or name added; both 10s Latin.

nativeness.note: plan.shared.h -2: «اشتراک کردہ» is stiff (reader r0 #8, r1 #6); kept under N733 because the fallback «کی اشتراک کی گئی» stacks «کی … کی» and the loan «شیئر» is refused (P16-test). plan.routeLimit -2: the heavy participle «کھلنے والے راستے» is gone (N739), but «پڑاؤ» can read as a camp (N734 binds) and «قبول کرتا ہے» is a software verb that two readers took for a calque. plan.empty.d -1: «چنیں» for acting on a button is the line's neutral verb, not the everyday phone word. Published phrases «اس آلے پر», «بنا بنایا راستہ پا لیں», «محفوظ کردہ» are chatty or official but bind by sibling consistency.

termbase_style.note: plan.shared.h -1: «اشتراک کردہ» participle of the N3 verb, no termbase entry of its own. «پڑاؤ» is still status pending (no dictionary page read in the line). Letterforms, digits, punctuation, quotes, P22 pronouns, P2 head name, brands and P16-admitted loans all clean (stage 5 list and verify.mjs OK).

fit_for_traveller.note: -1: the shared-list box (paragraph plus «میرے محفوظ کردہ مقامات دیکھیں») can be misread as viewing the shared list; that is the source's design (SD-M2) and the Urdu keeps faith. Labels are short, the counter reads as a count line, the confirm is one question ending in «؟».

The clause says what the English («the route opens with the first 10 sights on your list») and the Arabic («فيُفتح المسار بأول 10 معالم في قائمتك») say, with the finite verb of the button plan.route («گوگل میپس پر راستہ کھولیں»), so the note and the button speak of the same route. It removes the participle that two fresh readers stumbled on (r0 #13 'heavy'; r1 #10 'a road that opens') and the doubled «راستے … راستے». It adds no number, no 'only', no destination and no fact; both 10s stay Latin; «راستہ» and «پڑاؤ» stay per N734. Not taken from the readers: «اسٹاپ» (loan, P16-test (1) fails), «اجازت دیتا ہے» (a modal shift from 'accepts'), and any sentence saying which 10 or what happens to the rest (neither source says; SD-M1: the page has no order control).
rulings.evidence: blind-reader.r0.md #13; blind-reader.r1.md #9, #10; pack.json plan.routeLimit (en, ar, ctx); judge-r1.json N734 note and [j1] item 54.

source_defects.defect: The English 'Arrange them' and the Arabic «رتّبها» promise arranging, but the page has no control that sorts or reorders (PlanView.astro: cards render in saved order; no sort, drag or reorder code). The 'first 10 sights on your list' of plan.routeLimit therefore depends on an order the visitor cannot set, and 'ready-made route' promises more than the plain Google Maps directions link delivers (reader r0 #4, #5, #13; r1 #2, #10). The Urdu keeps faith; the owner can drop 'Arrange them' from the three languages or add the control.

Shared-list mode (?list=): the box invites the visitor to 'browse it', but its only view button is 'View my saved places', which in the template (mine-btn) drops ?list= and returns to the visitor's own list; the H1 and the counter keep 'My saved places' / 'saved' while the cards are someone else's; what 'Add' does (merges the shared stops into the visitor's list, import-btn) is not said (reader r0 #9, serious; r1 #7). Source and template design; the Urdu keeps faith.

FIXED IN THE WORKING TREE (uncommitted). When read at round 1, PlanView.astro (tree fe0bab0 with local edits) had a ur branch in browseHref (/ur/attractions/) but none in mapHref, so the empty-state map button of the Urdu page fell through to /en/map/ instead of /ur/map/ (BRIEF names /ur/map/). At round 2, line 52 of PlanView.astro reads '… de ? '/de/map/' : ur ? '/ur/map/' : '/en/map/'' and git status shows the file modified, not committed: the fix reaches the site only when that edit is committed and merged.

The lead is passed as the page's meta description (Base description = t('plan.lead')) and also rendered under the H1, so a description and the visible lead are the same sentences (reader r0 #7); and the empty-state paragraph ends with the same 'get a ready route' as the lead, so the page says it twice (reader r1 #3). Template and source design; a separate plan.desc string would be needed for the first, and the second is in the English and Arabic.

Tab title = plan.title + titleSep + site.brand: the brand line stays the Latin wordmark and the separator is the template's (reader r0 #1, r1 #17). This is the open item BRAND (N1), the owner's to decide; the reader also asks that the tab title say the list is the visitor's own, which the single string plan.title cannot do.

No user-facing message exists for: a failed clipboard write (the script swallows the error and shows nothing), a failed share or Maps open, an invalid or empty ?list= (silently shows the visitor's own list), or undo after «ہٹائیں» (reader r0 #20). The copy success text exists (published ui plan.copied). Nothing can be added in Urdu; a string and template change would be needed.

The sources disagree on kind: en 'Location ↗' and ar «الموقع ↗» are a noun, while the approved zh line is an action (在谷歌地图中打开 ↗, 'open in Google Maps') and the de/ru are nouns. The Urdu follows en and ar (N731). If the owner wants the action reading on all languages, the English and Arabic change first.

English noun drift on one page: the title and buttons say 'places', the counter and the shared heading say 'sights' (the ctx example even reads '{n} saved places'); recorded at s1. The Urdu keeps the published pair «سیاحتی مقامات» / «مقامات» per string.
